cures.text: After being sealed with polyethylene film, it was first cured at 60 °C for 6 h and continued at room temperature for 7 days.

results.ageNote: test age not stated: sealed, 6 h at 60 °C, then 7 days at room temperature
results.text: When the phosphoric acid concentration was 12 mol/L, the SFCC catalyst-based geopolymer obtained the highest compressive strength of 30.2 MPa, which is even higher than that of metakaolin-based geopolymer with the same condition.

results.ageNote: test age not stated: sealed, 6 h at 60 °C, then 7 days at room temperature
results.text: With the acid concentration decreasing from 12 to 6 mol/L, the compressive strength of geopolymers decreased from 30.2 MPa to 9.8 MPa.

results.ageNote: test age not stated: sealed, 6 h at 60 °C, then 7 days at room temperature
results.text: However, at a higher acid concentration of 14 mol, it almost could not condense and harden to form geopolymer, and the compressive strength was only 1.2 MPa.

findings.text: When the phosphoric acid concentration was 12 mol/L, the SFCC catalyst-based geopolymer obtained the highest compressive strength of 30.2 MPa, which is even higher than that of metakaolin-based geopolymer with the same condition.

notes.text: However, at a higher acid concentration of 14 mol, it almost could not condense and harden to form geopolymer, and the compressive strength was only 1.2 MPa.

gaps: Table quotes follow the standard form; the 40 mL acid volume is one cell spanning specimens 1–5 in the source (specimen 6 has its own cell).

Specimen numbers are the paper's labels (Table 2 'Specimen No.'; the text uses 'No. 2', 'No. 4', 'No. 6'); because the strength sentences name acid concentrations, each specimen's concentration is recorded as its alias.
Strengths at 8 and 10 mol/L and for the metakaolin comparison (No. 6) are only in Figure 2; the text says only that No. 4 exceeds the metakaolin specimen.
The acid solution was prepared from 85% H3PO4 and deionized water; the acid mass per batch is not given. Test age is not stated.
